parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Both services cover fleet-workshop work, so the topic holds together. The way they are built does not.

1. Different data-access abstractions. MaintenanceService works through the table classes (VehicleTable, WorkOrderTable). It calls row/write/insert/openFor, rebuilds Vehicle and WorkOrder domain objects, and reports errors as FleetError. MileageService skips that layer: it takes the raw PrismaService and calls prisma.mileage.create and prisma.mileage.findMany directly. It also never uses the Vehicle model or FleetError.

2. The service-due rule lives outside the model. Vehicle owns the service state (lastServiceKm, returnToService) and exports SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM. MileageService.record recomputes the rule itself, as `km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM`, using a lastServiceKm the caller passes in. It does not load the Vehicle and ask it. So the rule exists in a second place, and it trusts a caller-supplied value instead of the stored one, which MaintenanceService.close updates.

3. Inconsistent invariants. MaintenanceService checks that the vehicle exists and throws FleetError(404) if not. MileageService.record writes readings for any plate without checking.

Confidence is moderate because the Vehicle model's source isn't included, so I can't confirm it already has a service-due method.

violations.message: Skips the module's table/repository abstraction: it injects PrismaService and calls prisma.mileage.create/findMany directly. MaintenanceService works only through VehicleTable and WorkOrderTable.

record() re-implements the service-due rule (`km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM`) outside the Vehicle model, using a caller-supplied lastServiceKm instead of the stored Vehicle state, so the rule is in two places.
Doesn't follow the module's checks: it records mileage for unknown plates without the vehicle-existence check and FleetError(404) that MaintenanceService.vehicle() enforces.
